videos.title: The Observability Layer for the Physical World
videos.description:
Tractian (YC W21) is building physical AI for asset-heavy industries, helping factories and industrial operators monitor critical equipment, predict failures, and prevent costly downtime. Their platform combines proprietary sensors, software, and AI to monitor hundreds of thousands of assets in real time. 

They’ve now crossed $100 million in ARR, growing 90% year over year, and recently raised a $130M Series D at a $1.4B valuation.

In this Founder Fireside, co-founder and CEO Igor Marinelli joins YC’s Harj Taggar to share how Tractian grew from a problem he first saw through his father’s work as a plant manager into a platform used by some of the world’s largest industrial companies. They dig into how Tractian won its first enterprise customers, why AI is changing the economics of industrial maintenance, and how the company is moving from monitoring machines toward a future where factories can increasingly operate themselves.

https://tractian.com

videos.name: Y Combinator
videos.title: Stop Wasting AI Tokens
videos.description:
Weave (YC W25) helps engineering teams understand whether their AI coding tools are actually making them more productive. Its models measure the work humans and agents produce and compare that output with AI spending. The company recently raised a $13.5M Series A led by Standard Capital and launched Weave Router, which selects models for different coding tasks.

In this Fireside, co-founders Adam Cohen and Andrew Churchill discuss how they went from measuring human productivity to optimizing coding agents, why cost per output matters more than raw token spend, and how their AI coach helps engineers work more effectively with agents. They also share their vision for autonomous software factories and explain why combining different models’ strengths could outperform any single model.

https://weaveos.com

videos.title: Behind Latent Space: Kill My SaaS, Jev & AI in 2026 | AIEi Shanghai
videos.description:
Galen Gao (https://substack.com/@linkloud1, https://x.com/Ninggao88) interviews Shawn Wang (swyx) ahead of AIEi Shanghai, the first AI Engineer conference in China. They talk about how a blog on open-source AI became Latent Space, how the AI Engineer community grew, and what local builders brought to Shanghai.

Then they get into Kill My SaaS. An agent can rebuild a tool and pass the entry checks. Choosing a winner still takes someone who knows what an organizer needs to get done. The conversation also covers OpenClaw adoption in China and what Thinking Machines' interaction models change about talking to AI.

videos.name: Latent Space
videos.title: ⚡️ The 2026 Software Factory Infra Stack — Zach Lloyd, Warp.dev
videos.description:
Software factories at Warp: founder and CEO Zach Lloyd walks swyx through the system his team uses to turn tasks into pull requests, measure agent quality, and improve the workflow itself.

The demo follows a request from Slack to a PR, then explores shared agent traces, cost and throughput scoring, and benchmarks built from real engineering work. Zach reports that tuning models and subagent use brought Warp’s internal cost from about $80 per PR to roughly $15–20, alongside higher throughput.

How do software factories change the work of product engineers? What belongs in a benchmark? And how can agents help improve the factory that runs them?

Join Zach and the AI engineering community at AIE CODE, November 10–12, 2026 in San Francisco. Apply to attend: https://ai.engineer/code/2026
